Hi Sara / Acme security team,

Thanks for the heads-up on the questionnaire. As requested, please find attached a concise pack to kick off your evaluation: our current subprocessor list (rows include region, data category, contract link), a short SOC 2 Type II summary, and a diagram of our key management boundaries.

Quick notes to help you triage:
- The subprocessor list is the canonical list for production data handling; rows marked "sensitive" indicate processors that touch PHI/ePHI in customer deployments.
- We operate with customer-isolated peering in our Private offering; default hosted deployments are multi-tenant but have encryption at rest + in transit.
- For key control, we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private and Redwood-managed keys for hosted — see the KMS diagram.

What would help us move faster from your side: a short prioritized list of items you want evidence for (e.g., contract redlines, encryption control descriptions, SOC 2 artifacts) and whether you need us to route anything through procurement or legal.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-list-2024-11.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOC2-Type2-summary-2024.pdf (summary), redwood-kms-diagram.png

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

—Marissa

Sara / team, Vivek here (Head of Applied Security Ops). Two quick technical clarifications to save time:

1) Encryption at rest: for hosted customers we use AES-256 with provider-managed keys by default; we will provide Customer KMS integration docs and the HSM-KMS boundary diagram for Dedicated/Private. If you require FIPS 140-2 validated HSM detail, let us know and we can surface the boundary/attestation artifacts.

2) Tokenization vs plaintext: we use a tokenization layer for sensitive identifiers prior to longer-term storage for customers who opt-in; Procuro Analytics performs ephemeral decryption in a transient processing VPC for analytics only, and we log and monitor those sessions. We will provide a short bulleted procedure and sample audit log extract showing the ephemeral decryption session ID format.

3) Supply chain vetting: Redwood maintains a quarterly risk review for our top-15 subprocessors (coverage includes vulnerability scanning posture, dependency SBOM if applicable, and contract SLAs). We will export the last review summary for Procuro and two other critical suppliers.

I’ve attached our SOC2-Type2-summary-2024.pdf and a snippet of the KMS diagram. Let us know if you need specific control IDs mapped to SIG items — we can tranche that work into a follow-up.

—Vivek
